claims.text: Molecular dynamics simulations can be used to study the thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles as a function of particle size.
FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles exhibit a size-dependent thermal response.
Smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles have lower thermal stability than larger FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles.
Lower thermal stability in smaller nanoparticles manifests as a lower effective melting or transformation temperature.
An empirical potential that captures multicomponent interactions is appropriate for MD heating simulations of FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles.
Using identical heating conditions across particle sizes isolates the effect of nanoparticle size.
The surface-to-volume ratio affects atomic mobility and local bonding fluctuations.
Surface-to-volume-ratio effects mediate the thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles.
Smaller nanoparticles have a higher fraction of surface atoms.
A higher surface-atom fraction enhances atomic mobility.
Enhanced atomic mobility causes an earlier onset of melting or restructuring in smaller nanoparticles.
Energy fluctuations and structural order-parameter changes in MD simulations can identify the onset of melting or restructuring.
Larger nanoparticles or bulk FeCuCrCoNi material have higher thermal stability because surface effects are weaker.
The predicted size dependence is sensitive to the accuracy of the interatomic potential.
MD simulations may omit experimental effects such as oxidation and external stresses.
Potential-energy changes, radial distribution functions, specific-heat peaks, and structural order parameters can be used as indicators of thermal disordering or melting.
